# Some Preparations {.hidden .unnumbered .unlisted}
```{r}
# Compute all sample-derived objects from a given sample selection: filtered data, block-level
# (alpha, eta) estimates, the alpha/eta summary tables and the OHI_table. Defined as a function so
# the exact same pipeline serves both the main sample and the sensitivity samples (fully-rational,
# synthetic-fill, unipref; see the driver chunk after the panel definitions). Returns every object
# it creates - including the helper functions retrieve_alphas()/nthroot()/calculate_OHI_score() -
# as a list, which the caller exposes via list2env() for the downstream chunks.
compute_prep <- function(main_sample_subject_selection, unipref_eta = NULL, synthetic_fill = FALSE) {
# Filter data for main sample selection
data_decision_task_online <- data_decision_task_online_raw %>% filter(paste(participant_code, block_number) %in% paste(main_sample_subject_selection$participant_code, main_sample_subject_selection$task_number))
ohi_estimates_online <- ohi_estimates_online_raw %>% filter(paste(participant_code, task_number) %in% paste(main_sample_subject_selection$participant_code, main_sample_subject_selection$task_number))

# Unipref sensitivity override: for the re-included corner-solution blocks (unipref != 0),
# assign alpha = 1/0 by the almost-exclusively-chosen goal (mean share to goal1 > 0.5 -> 1, else 0)
# and a fixed substitutability eta (0 or 100). Only runs when unipref_eta is supplied, so the main
# and fully-rational passes are unaffected.
if (!is.null(unipref_eta)) {
    dominant_goal_alpha <- data_decision_task_online %>%
        group_by(participant_code, block_number) %>%
        summarise(share_goal1 = mean(to_goal1 / (to_goal1 + to_goal2), na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
        transmute(participant_code, task_number = block_number,
                  assigned_alpha = ifelse(share_goal1 > 0.5, 1, 0))
    ohi_estimates_online <- ohi_estimates_online %>%
        left_join(dominant_goal_alpha, by = c("participant_code", "task_number")) %>%
        mutate(alpha = ifelse(!is.na(unipref) & unipref != 0, assigned_alpha, alpha),
               eta   = ifelse(!is.na(unipref) & unipref != 0, unipref_eta,    eta)) %>%
        select(-assigned_alpha)
}

# Optionally balance observation counts per participant by synthetic filling (up to three blocks
# each, so every subject carries equal weight in the pooled eta). OFF for the main analysis, which
# uses the existing observations as-is; ON only for the appendix Fig. 2e sensitivity panel that
# reproduces the previous equal-participant-weight behaviour.
if (synthetic_fill) {
    ohi_estimates_online <- ohi_estimates_online %>%
      group_by(participant_code) %>%
      mutate(n_obs = n()) %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      nest(data = -c(participant_code, n_obs)) %>%
      mutate(data = purrr::map2(data, n_obs, function(df, n) {
        if (n == 3) {
          return(df)
        } else if (n == 2) {
          # For 2 observations, create one new row with mean eta and no alpha
          new_row <- df %>% slice(1) %>% mutate(eta = mean(df$eta, na.rm = TRUE), task_number = NA, alpha = NA, task_name = NA, rho = NA, sigma = NA, nllsq_alpha = NA, unipref = NA)
          return(bind_rows(df, new_row))
        } else if (n == 1) {
          # For 1 observation, create two new rows with same eta and no alpha
          new_rows <- df %>% slice(c(1, 1)) %>% mutate(task_number = NA, alpha = NA, task_name = NA, rho = NA, sigma = NA, nllsq_alpha = NA, unipref = NA)
          return(bind_rows(df, new_rows))
        } else {
          return(df)
        }
      })) %>%
      select(-n_obs) %>%
      unnest(data)
}

# English goal names for the pairwise task labels (used by the panels and downstream chunks)
replace_vector <- goal_names$goal_code_eng
names(replace_vector) <- goal_names$goal_code
ohi_estimates_online_eng <- ohi_estimates_online %>% mutate(task_name = str_replace_all(task_name, pattern = replace_vector))

# Function that estimates the underlying alpha weights from the pairwise comparison data
retrieve_alphas <- function(dataset) { # dataset = subset of ohi_estimates_online
    # na.omit drops the eta-only synthetic balancing rows (present in the synthetic_fill pass),
    # which carry no alpha and play no role in the alpha estimation
    dataset <- na.omit(dataset)
    # Replace the goal pair names with the english goal names in the grid & dataset
    replace_vector <- c(goal_names$goal_code_eng)
    names(replace_vector) <- c(goal_names$goal_code)
    dataset <- dataset %>%
        mutate(task_name = str_replace_all(task_name, pattern = replace_vector))

    median_estimates <- dataset %>%
        tidyr::separate_wider_delim(task_name, delim = "-", names = c("goal1", "goal2")) %>%
        group_by(goal1, goal2) %>%
        summarize(median_alpha = round(median(alpha, na.rm = TRUE), 2))

    # Retrieve approximation for global alpha weights from goal-pair median alphas
    alpha_ratio_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = length(goals), ncol = length(goals),
                        dimnames = list(goals, goals))

    # Fill matrix with alpha-ratios
    for (g1 in goals) {
        for (g2 in goals) {
            a_i <- median_estimates$median_alpha[median_estimates$goal1 == g1 & median_estimates$goal2 == g2]
            a_j <- 1 - a_i
            if (length(a_i) == 1 && length(a_j) == 1 && !is.na(a_i) && !is.na(a_j) && a_j != 0) {
                alpha_ratio_mat[g1, g2] <- a_i / a_j
            } else if (g1 == g2) {
                alpha_ratio_mat[g1, g2] <- 1
            }
        }
    }

    # Apply geometric mean type formula of Hovanov et al. (2008)
    n_items <- nrow(alpha_ratio_mat)
    alpha_weights <- sapply(seq_len(n_items), function(i) {
      numer <- alpha_ratio_mat[i, ]        # C_i1 ... C_in
      denom <- alpha_ratio_mat[, i]        # C_1i ... C_ni
      ratio <- numer / denom               # C_ij / C_ji

      # Validity check
      valid <- ratio[!is.na(ratio) & is.finite(ratio) & (ratio > 0)]

      if(length(valid) == 0) {
        return(NA_real_)
      }

      # Apply formula
      exp((1 / (2 * n_items)) * sum(log(valid)))
    })
    names(alpha_weights) <- rownames(alpha_ratio_mat)

    # Normalize weights to sum to 1
    alpha_weights <- alpha_weights / sum(alpha_weights, na.rm = TRUE)

    # Turn named vector into a dataframe
    alpha_weights <- tibble::tibble(
      goal = names(alpha_weights),
      alpha_median = as.numeric(alpha_weights)
    )

    return(alpha_weights)
}

# Retrieve total sample alpha weights
alpha_total_sample <- retrieve_alphas(ohi_estimates_online)

# Retrieve country level alpha weights
estimates_wcountry <- ohi_estimates_online %>%
    inner_join(
        y = data_decision_task_online[ , c("participant_code", "session_label")],
        by = c("participant_code"),
        multiple = "any") %>%
    inner_join(
        y = country_abrv,
        by = c("session_label")) %>%
    select(-session_label)

alpha_per_country <- tibble(goal = goal_names$goal_name)

for(country in unique(estimates_wcountry$country_abrv)) { 
    current_data <- estimates_wcountry %>% 
        filter(country_abrv == country)

    country_results <- retrieve_alphas(current_data) %>%
        mutate(goal = goal_names$goal_name[goal_names$goal_code_eng == goal],
               !!country := as.character(round(alpha_median, 3))) %>%
        select(-alpha_median)

    alpha_per_country <- alpha_per_country %>% # Add results for current country to final table
        left_join(
            y = country_results,
            by = c("goal"))
}
    
# Country Level Eta Hypotheses-Tests
eta_per_country <- tibble( # Initiate empty table for all tests
    Country = character(),
    pValue = numeric(),
    MeanEta = numeric(),
    StdError = numeric(),
    Median = numeric()
)

for(country in unique(estimates_wcountry$country_abrv)) { # Run t-test for each country
    current_ttest_data <- estimates_wcountry %>% 
        filter(country_abrv == country)

    current_ttest <- t.test(current_ttest_data$eta, mu = 0, alternative = "two.sided")

    eta_per_country <- eta_per_country %>%
        add_row(Country = country,
                pValue = round(current_ttest$p.value, 2),
                MeanEta = round(current_ttest$estimate, 1),
                StdError = round(current_ttest$stderr, 1),
                Median = round(median(current_ttest_data$eta), 3)
                )
}

current_ttest <- t.test(estimates_wcountry$eta, mu = 0, alternative = "two.sided") # Add overall t-test to table

eta_per_country <- eta_per_country %>%
    add_row(Country = "All",
            pValue = round(current_ttest$p.value, 2),
            MeanEta = round(current_ttest$estimate, 1),
            StdError = round(current_ttest$stderr, 1),
            Median = round(median(estimates_wcountry$eta), 3)
            )

# Drop loop temporaries so they do not end up in the returned prep list
rm(list = c('country_results', 'current_ttest_data', 'current_ttest', 'country'))

eta_total_sample <- ohi_estimates_online$eta %>%
    median()

nthroot = function(x,n) {
  (abs(x)^(1/n))*sign(x)
}

calculate_OHI_score <- function(alpha_vector, score_vector, eta) { # Both vectors have to be sorted in descending alphabetical order in terms of the goal names
    ifelse(eta == 1, return(nthroot(prod(score_vector ^ (alpha_vector)), sum(alpha_vector))), return(sum(alpha_vector * (score_vector ^ (1-eta))) ^ (1/(1-eta))))
}

# Obtain a table with the total country scores in 2022
base_OHI_2022 <- ohi_scores %>% 
  filter(scenario == 2022,
         goal == "Index",
         dimension == "score") %>%
  filter(!is.na(value)) %>% 
  select(region_name, value) %>%
  mutate(rank = rank(-value, ties.method = "min"))

# Obtain a table with all OHI scores by goal and country in 2022
OHI_scores_2022_goallevel <- ohi_scores %>%
    filter(scenario == 2022,
         goal %in% goal_names$goal_code_eng,
         dimension == "score") %>%
         arrange(goal) 

# Manually add the missing data on TR for Japan & Australia: the OHI website shows both with a score
# of 100 for all years up to 2022 (that is, all years before pandemic data is incorporated)
OHI_scores_2022_goallevel <- OHI_scores_2022_goallevel %>%
    mutate(value = ifelse(region_name %in% c("Japan", "Australia") & goal == "TR", 100, value))

# Throw out all countries that have some missing goal score
OHI_scores_2022_goallevel <- OHI_scores_2022_goallevel %>%
       group_by(region_name) %>%
       filter(!any(is.na(value))) %>%
       ungroup()

# Replace german goal names with english goal abbreviations and transform to long format
alpha_allcountries_goallevel <- alpha_per_country %>% 
    mutate(goal = goal_names$goal_code_eng[match(goal, goal_names$goal_name)]) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = -goal, names_to = "region_name", values_to = "alpha_median") %>%
    mutate(alpha_median = as.numeric(alpha_median)) %>%
    mutate(region_name = country_abrv$region_name[match(region_name, country_abrv$country_abrv)])

# Join the alpha and eta values with the OHI scores
OHI_table <- OHI_scores_2022_goallevel %>%
    full_join( # Join OHI scores with alpha values
        y = alpha_allcountries_goallevel,
        by = c('goal', 'region_name')) %>%
        select(goal, region_name, value, alpha_median) %>%
        mutate(country_code = country_abrv$country_abrv[match(region_name, country_abrv$region_name)]) %>%
        rename(country=region_name, score=value) %>%
    full_join( # Join OHI scores with eta values (per-country medians for surveyed countries; others get the overall median below)
        y = eta_per_country[, c('Country', 'Median')],
        join_by(country_code == Country)) %>%
        rename(eta_median = Median)

# All Countries that are not part of the survey get overall median & eta values
OHI_table <- OHI_table %>%
    mutate(eta_median = ifelse(is.na(eta_median), eta_total_sample, eta_median)) %>%
    mutate(alpha_median = ifelse(is.na(alpha_median), alpha_total_sample$alpha_median[match(goal, alpha_total_sample$goal)], alpha_median))

# Calculate adjusted OHI scores
OHI_table <- OHI_table %>%
    group_by(country) %>%
    mutate(adjusted_OHI = calculate_OHI_score(alpha_median, score, eta_median)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(rank = dense_rank(adjusted_OHI))

# Add base OHI scores and rename columns
OHI_table <- OHI_table %>%
    left_join(
        y = base_OHI_2022,
        by = c("country" = "region_name")) %>%
    select(-c(rank.x, rank.y)) %>% # Drop ranks as these are recalculated in the next step
    rename(base_OHI = value,
        goal_score = score)

# Determine ranks for each country (workaround as ties could come from both duplicate rows and equal country scores)
OHI_table_ranks <- OHI_table %>%
    filter(country != "Global average") %>% # Don't rank the global average
    distinct(country, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(base_rank = rank(-base_OHI, ties.method = "min")) %>%
    mutate(adjusted_rank = rank(-adjusted_OHI, ties.method = "min")) %>%
    select(country, base_rank, adjusted_rank)

# Join ranks with OHI table
OHI_table <- OHI_table %>%
    left_join(
        y = OHI_table_ranks,
        by = c("country")) %>%
    relocate(c("country_code", "country", "goal", "goal_score", "alpha_median", "eta_median", "base_OHI", "adjusted_OHI", "base_rank", "adjusted_rank")) %>%
    arrange(country) %>%
    filter(is.na(country_code)|country_code!="All") # Remove 'All' row (workaround as filter usually excludes all NA values, which we don't want here)

# Return every object created above so the caller can reuse them (panels + downstream chunks)
return(as.list(environment()))
}
```

# Start plotting figures {.hidden .unnumbered .unlisted}
```{r}
# Build Main Panel Figures 2, 3 and 4 from a prep list (see compute_prep()). output_suffix is ""
# for the main sample and "_FullyRational" for the sensitivity sample; it is appended to the saved
# PDF filenames. All three panels live in one function so figure-internal objects (goal_colors,
# replace_vector, un_gdp_data, ohi_estimates_online_eng, ...) are shared exactly as they were when
# the panels ran as consecutive chunks.
build_all_panels <- function(prep, output_suffix) {
list2env(prep, environment())

### Panel Figure 2: Index aggregation preferences and reweighting of OHI scores

## Panel A - Alpha Weighting
# Define color palette for each goal abbreviation
goal_colors <- c(
    "FP" = "#98234A",
    "AO" = "#EC6A5A",
    "NP" = "#F07E58",
    "CS" = "#F39A67",
    "CP" = "#F6B376",
    "LE" = "#EFE498",
    "TR" = "#FAD08A",
    "SP" = "#A7D6A8",
    "CW" = "#53A9B2",
    "BD" = "#4289BB"
)

# For text: test whether any goal's weight differs from equal weighting (1/N = 0.1), via a
# studentized (bootstrap-t) test with a nested bootstrap:
#   - B_outer resamples of the original data give theta*_b per goal.
#   - For each outer replicate, B_inner resamples (from that outer sample) give SE(theta*_b).
#   - A separate inner-style bootstrap on the original sample estimates SE(theta_hat).
#   - t*_b = (theta*_b - theta_hat) / SE(theta*_b); t_obs = (theta_hat - 0.1) / SE(theta_hat).
# No figure or table depends on this test and the nested bootstrap is computationally expensive
# (it runs in parallel on all available cores), so it is switched OFF by default. The paper
# reports results based on B_outer = 1000 and B_inner = 200 replicates; the smaller values below
# reduce the runtime for demonstration. Note: enabling the test advances the RNG and thereby
# changes the (purely cosmetic) point jitter in panels b and d of the main figure.
run_alpha_bootstrap <- FALSE

if (run_alpha_bootstrap) {
    library(foreach)
    library(doParallel)
    library(doRNG)

    B_outer <- 100
    B_inner <- 100

    one_resample_alphas <- function(data) {
        data %>%
            group_by(task_name) %>%
            slice_sample(prop = 1, replace = TRUE) %>%
            ungroup() %>%
            retrieve_alphas()
    }

    numCores <- parallel::detectCores()
    cl <- parallel::makeCluster(numCores)
    registerDoParallel(cl)
    registerDoRNG(123) # Set seed for reproducibility of parallel bootstrap

    worker_pkgs    <- c("dplyr", "tidyr", "tibble", "stringr", "purrr")
    worker_exports <- c("retrieve_alphas", "one_resample_alphas",
                        "ohi_estimates_online", "goal_names", "goals", "B_inner")

    # retrieve_alphas() is created inside compute_prep(), so it resolves goal_names and goals
    # lexically in the global environment of this session. foreach's .export only fills the
    # evaluation environment of the task, which is not on that lexical chain: on a worker the
    # lookup falls through to the worker's own (empty) global environment and the task fails with
    # "object 'goal_names' not found". clusterExport() puts the objects into each worker's global
    # environment, i.e. exactly where the chain ends, so it replaces .export here.
    parallel::clusterExport(cl, worker_exports, envir = environment())

    # Inner bootstrap on the original sample -> SE(theta_hat) per goal
    se_hat_inner <- foreach(
        s = seq_len(B_inner),
        .combine = bind_rows,
        .packages = worker_pkgs
    ) %dorng% {
        one_resample_alphas(ohi_estimates_online)
    }

    se_hat_per_goal <- se_hat_inner %>%
        group_by(goal) %>%
        summarize(se_hat = sd(alpha_median), .groups = "drop")

    # Outer loop with nested inner bootstrap for SE(theta*_b)
    outer_results <- foreach(
        b = seq_len(B_outer),
        .combine = bind_rows,
        .packages = worker_pkgs
    ) %dorng% {
        outer_sample <- ohi_estimates_online %>%
            group_by(task_name) %>%
            slice_sample(prop = 1, replace = TRUE) %>%
            ungroup()

        theta_star_b <- retrieve_alphas(outer_sample) %>%
            rename(theta_star = alpha_median)

        inner_df <- purrr::map_dfr(
            seq_len(B_inner),
            function(s) one_resample_alphas(outer_sample)
        )

        se_star_b <- inner_df %>%
            group_by(goal) %>%
            summarize(se_star = sd(alpha_median), .groups = "drop")

        theta_star_b %>% left_join(se_star_b, by = "goal") %>% mutate(outer_id = b)
    }

    stopCluster(cl)

    alpha_ttest_results <- tibble()
    for (goaltest in goal_names$goal_code_eng) {
        theta_hat <- alpha_total_sample$alpha_median[alpha_total_sample$goal == goaltest]
        se_hat   <- se_hat_per_goal$se_hat[se_hat_per_goal$goal == goaltest]

        goal_outer <- outer_results %>% filter(goal == goaltest)
        theta_star <- goal_outer$theta_star
        se_star    <- goal_outer$se_star

        # Drop replicates with degenerate SE (cannot studentize); count survivors for p-value
        keep <- is.finite(se_star) & se_star > 0
        t_star <- (theta_star[keep] - theta_hat) / se_star[keep]
        t_obs  <- (theta_hat - 0.1) / se_hat

        B <- length(t_star)
        n_le <- sum(t_star <= t_obs)
        n_ge <- sum(t_star >= t_obs)
        p_two <- min(1, 2 * min((1 + n_le) / (1 + B), (1 + n_ge) / (1 + B)))

        # Studentized (bootstrap-t) confidence interval: theta_hat - t_q * SE_hat,
        # with upper quantile mapped to the lower CI endpoint (and vice versa).
        t_q <- quantile(t_star, probs = c(0.975, 0.025), na.rm = TRUE)
        ci_low  <- theta_hat - t_q[1] * se_hat
        ci_high <- theta_hat - t_q[2] * se_hat

        alpha_ttest_results <- bind_rows(alpha_ttest_results, tibble(
            goal = goaltest,
            mean_alpha = mean(theta_star),
            median_alpha = median(theta_star),
            t_obs = t_obs,
            t_crit_low = unname(t_q[2]),
            t_crit_high = unname(t_q[1]),
            p_value = p_two,
            conf_low = unname(ci_low),
            conf_high = unname(ci_high)
        ))
    }

    print(alpha_ttest_results)  # H0: alpha_g = 0.1 for each goal g
}

## Panel A - Decomposition of OHI Score Change
panel_fig3_a_data <- OHI_table %>%
    mutate(eta_median = eta_total_sample) %>%

# Calculate partial & interaction effects
panel_fig3_a_data <- panel_fig3_a_data %>%
    group_by(country) %>%
    mutate(partialeffect_alpha = calculate_OHI_score(alpha_median, goal_score, rep(0, 10)) - base_OHI,
           partialeffect_eta = calculate_OHI_score(rep(0.1, 10), goal_score, eta_median) - base_OHI,
           partialeffect_alpha_winteract = calculate_OHI_score(alpha_median, goal_score, eta_median) - base_OHI - partialeffect_eta,
           partialeffect_eta_winteract = calculate_OHI_score(alpha_median, goal_score, eta_median) - base_OHI - partialeffect_alpha,
           pure_interactioneffect = partialeffect_eta_winteract - partialeffect_eta,) %>%
    ungroup()

## Panel B - Dynamic Country Differences (Timetrends Figure)
# Create Empty OHI Table for all years
OHI_table_allyears <- tibble()

# Loop through all years and create OHI table for all years
for (year in 2012:2024) {
    ## Prepare OHI Table for <year>
    # Obtain a table with the total country scores in <year>
    base_OHI_year <- ohi_scores %>% 
    filter(scenario == year,
            goal == "Index",
            dimension == "score") %>%
    filter(!is.na(value)) %>% 
    select(region_name, value) %>%
    mutate(rank = rank(-value, ties.method = "min"))

    # Obtain a table with all OHI scores by goal and country in <year>
    OHI_scores_year_goallevel <- ohi_scores %>%
        filter(scenario == year,
            goal %in% goal_names$goal_code_eng,
            dimension == "score") %>%
            arrange(goal) 

    # Throw out all countries that have some missing goal score
    OHI_scores_year_goallevel <- OHI_scores_year_goallevel %>%
        group_by(region_name) %>%
        filter(!any(is.na(value))) %>%
        ungroup()

    # Join the alpha and eta values with the OHI scores
    OHI_table_year <- OHI_scores_year_goallevel %>%
        full_join( # Join OHI scores with alpha values
            y = alpha_allcountries_goallevel,
            by = c('goal', 'region_name')) %>%
            select(goal, region_name, value, alpha_median) %>%
            mutate(country_code = country_abrv$country_abrv[match(region_name, country_abrv$region_name)]) %>%
            rename(country=region_name, score=value) %>%
        full_join( # Join OHI scores with eta values (per-country medians for surveyed countries; others get the overall median below)
            y = eta_per_country[, c('Country', 'Median')],
            join_by(country_code == Country)) %>%
            rename(eta_median = Median)

    # All Countries get country-specific, as well as overall median & eta values
    OHI_table_year <- OHI_table_year %>%
        mutate(eta_median = ifelse(is.na(eta_median), eta_total_sample, eta_median)) %>%
        mutate(alpha_median = ifelse(is.na(alpha_median), alpha_total_sample$alpha_median[match(goal, alpha_total_sample$goal)], alpha_median)) %>%
        mutate(eta_median_global = eta_total_sample) %>%
        mutate(alpha_median_global = alpha_total_sample$alpha_median[match(goal, alpha_total_sample$goal)])

    # Calculate adjusted OHI scores
    OHI_table_year <- OHI_table_year %>%
        group_by(country) %>%
        mutate(adjusted_OHI = calculate_OHI_score(alpha_median, score, eta_median)) %>%
        mutate(adjusted_OHI_global = calculate_OHI_score(alpha_median_global, score, eta_median_global)) %>%
        ungroup() %>%
        mutate(rank = dense_rank(adjusted_OHI))

    # Add base OHI scores and rename columns
    OHI_table_year <- OHI_table_year %>%
        left_join(
            y = base_OHI_year,
            by = c("country" = "region_name")) %>%
        select(-c(rank.x, rank.y)) %>% # Drop ranks as these are recalculated in the next step
        rename(base_OHI = value,
            goal_score = score)

    # Determine ranks for each country (workaround as ties could come from both duplicate rows and equal country scores)
    OHI_table_year_ranks <- OHI_table_year %>%
        filter(country != "Global average") %>% # Don't rank the global average
        distinct(country, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
        mutate(base_rank = rank(-base_OHI, ties.method = "min")) %>%
        mutate(adjusted_rank = rank(-adjusted_OHI, ties.method = "min")) %>%
        select(country, base_rank, adjusted_rank)

    # Join ranks with OHI table
    OHI_table_year <- OHI_table_year %>%
        left_join(
            y = OHI_table_year_ranks,
            by = c("country")) %>%
        relocate(c("country_code", "country", "goal", "goal_score", "alpha_median", "eta_median", "alpha_median_global", "eta_median_global", "base_OHI", "adjusted_OHI", "adjusted_OHI_global", "base_rank", "adjusted_rank")) %>%
        arrange(country) %>%
        filter(is.na(country_code)|country_code!="All") # Remove 'All' row (workaround as filter usually excludes all NA values, which we don't want here)

    OHI_table_year <- OHI_table_year %>%
        mutate(year = as.character(year)) %>%
        select(year, everything())
    
    # Add row for overall goal for each country
    OHI_table_year <- OHI_table_year %>%
        bind_rows(
            OHI_table_year %>%
            filter(!country == "Global average") %>% # Don't include 'All' or 'Global average' in overall goal
            group_by(country) %>%
            summarise(
                goal = "Overall",
                goal_score = NA,
                alpha_median = NA,
                eta_median = NA,
                alpha_median_global = NA,
                eta_median_global = NA,
                base_OHI = mean(base_OHI, na.rm = TRUE),
                adjusted_OHI = mean(adjusted_OHI, na.rm = TRUE),
                adjusted_OHI_global = mean(adjusted_OHI_global, na.rm = TRUE),
                base_rank = base_rank[1],
                adjusted_rank = adjusted_rank[1]
            ) %>%
            ungroup()
        ) %>% # Throw out all countries that have missing values (i.e. Australia and Japan)
        filter(!is.na(base_OHI) & !is.na(adjusted_OHI))

    # Add mean base/adjusted OHI scores for the year
    OHI_table_year <- OHI_table_year %>%
        bind_rows(
            tibble(
                year = as.character(year),
                country_code = "All",
                country = "Global average",
                goal = "Overall",
                goal_score = NA,
                alpha_median = NA,
                eta_median = NA,
                alpha_median_global = NA,
                eta_median_global = NA,
                base_OHI = mean(OHI_table_year$base_OHI, na.rm = TRUE),
                adjusted_OHI = mean(OHI_table_year$adjusted_OHI, na.rm = TRUE),
                adjusted_OHI_global = mean(OHI_table_year$adjusted_OHI_global, na.rm = TRUE),
                base_rank = NA,
                adjusted_rank = NA
            )
        )

    # Select only the relevant columns
    OHI_table_year <- OHI_table_year %>%
        filter(goal == "Overall") %>% # Only keep "overall" goal
        select(country_code, country, base_OHI, adjusted_OHI, adjusted_OHI_global, base_rank, adjusted_rank) %>%
        mutate(year = as.character(year)) %>% # Ensure year is set
        select(year, everything()) # Move year to the first column

    # Append to OHI table for all years
    OHI_table_allyears <- bind_rows(OHI_table_allyears, OHI_table_year) 
}
```

```{r}
# ---- Generate Main Panel Figures 2-4 (main sample) + Fig. 2e sensitivity figure ----

# Main sample: build the figures and expose the prep objects for the downstream (SI Appendix) chunks.
main_prep <- compute_prep(main_sample_subject_selection)
list2env(main_prep, envir = environment())
set.seed(123) # Reproduce the main figures (Panel 2 uses jitter(), which draws on the RNG)
# Capture the (unchanged) main-sample panel objects so the Krinsky-Robb CI figure below can re-use
# them; the main figure itself is built and saved inside build_all_panels exactly as before.
main_panels <- build_all_panels(main_prep, "")
main_rng_state <- .Random.seed # Remember the RNG state so the downstream figures stay reproducible

# Sensitivity prep lists (Fig. 2e only):
#  - fully-rational sample: participants without a single excluded decision block (built in
#    05_Sample_Selection.qmd)
#  - synthetic-fill sample: the MAIN sample with synthetic balancing switched on (each
#    participant filled up to three blocks).
#  - unipref: re-include the previously-excluded corner-solution blocks with assigned alpha (1/0 by
#    dominant goal) and a fixed substitutability eta. Two bounding versions: eta = 0 (perfect
#    substitutes) and eta = 100 (near-Leontief).
fully_rational_sample_selection <- read_csv(here::here("1_Data", "2_processed", "main_sample_selection_fullyrational.csv"))
fully_rational_prep <- compute_prep(fully_rational_sample_selection)
synthetic_fill_prep <- compute_prep(main_sample_subject_selection, synthetic_fill = TRUE)
unipref_sample_selection <- read_csv(here::here("1_Data", "2_processed", "main_sample_selection_unipref.csv"))
unipref_eta0_prep   <- compute_prep(unipref_sample_selection, unipref_eta = 0)
unipref_eta100_prep <- compute_prep(unipref_sample_selection, unipref_eta = 100)

# Density panel of base vs. adjusted country scores, with mean markers, the mean-change arrow and
# the %-change label (all computed exactly as in the main Fig. 2e, which keeps its own unchanged
# code inside build_all_panels). Mirrors the main panel_fig2_e but adds a panel title and a compact
# legend so several panels read cleanly when stacked. `d` needs one row per country with columns
# base_OHI and adjusted_OHI; `pct_x` positions the %-change label. Reused by the Fig. 2e sensitivity
# stacks in SI Appendix Figs. S4 and S8.
plot_ohi_density_panel <- function(d, panel_title, pct_x = 63) {
  ggplot() +
    geom_density(data = d, aes(x = base_OHI), color = "#D55E00", fill = "#D55E00", alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_density(data = d, aes(x = adjusted_OHI), color = "#009E73", fill = "#009E73", alpha = 0.4) +
    # Mean base_OHI
    geom_segment(data = d, aes(x = mean(base_OHI), xend = mean(base_OHI), y = 0, yend = 0.1, color = "Baseline", linetype = "Mean"), linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_text(data = d, aes(x = mean(base_OHI), y = 0.1, label = round(mean(base_OHI), 0)), vjust = -0.5, hjust = 0.5, size = 7 /.pt, check_overlap = TRUE) +
    # Mean adjusted_OHI
    geom_segment(data = d, aes(x = mean(adjusted_OHI), xend = mean(adjusted_OHI), y = 0, yend = 0.1, color = "Adjusted", linetype = "Mean"), linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_text(data = d, aes(x = mean(adjusted_OHI), y = 0.1, label = round(mean(adjusted_OHI), 0)), vjust = -0.5, hjust = 0.7, size = 7 /.pt, check_overlap = TRUE) +
    # Line with arrow + %-change label (identical computation to the main Fig. 2e)
    geom_segment(data = d, aes(x = mean(adjusted_OHI), xend = mean(base_OHI), y = 0.095, yend = 0.095),
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.1, "cm"), ends = "first", type = "open", angle = 30), linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_text(data = d, aes(x = pct_x, y = 0.096, label = paste0(round((1 - mean(adjusted_OHI) / mean(base_OHI)) * -100), "%")),
              vjust = 0, hjust = 0, size = 7 /.pt, check_overlap = TRUE) +
    labs(x = "OHI score", y = "Density", title = panel_title) +
    scale_x_continuous(limit = c(0, 100), expand = c(0, 0), breaks = seq(0, 100, 10)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limit = c(0, 0.11), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_color_manual(breaks = c("Baseline", "Adjusted"), values = c("Baseline" = "#D55E00", "Adjusted" = "#009E73")) +
    scale_linetype_manual(breaks = c("Median", "Mean"), values = c("Median" = "solid", "Mean" = "dashed")) +
    theme_basic +
    theme(
        plot.title = element_text(size = 8, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 2)),
        legend.position = "inside",
        legend.position.inside = c(0.13, 0.62),
        legend.background = element_blank(),
        legend.title = element_blank(),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
        legend.spacing.x = unit(0, "mm"),
        legend.spacing.y = unit(-3, "mm"),
        legend.key.height = unit(0.6, "lines"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, vjust = 6, size = 7),
        axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 7),
        plot.margin = unit(c(0, 0, 0, 0), "cm"),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 7),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 7),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.length = unit(0.1, "cm"),
        axis.ticks.x = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3),
        axis.ticks.y = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3),
        axis.line.x = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.3),
        axis.line.y = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.3)
    )
}

# Rebuild ONLY the Fig. 2e panel for a given sensitivity prep list; the main published Figure 2 is
```

```{r}
# ---- Figure 2 with Krinsky-Robb confidence intervals (parameter-uncertainty SENSITIVITY analysis) ----
# Separate from the main Figure 2 (left unchanged). For every main-sample block we draw
# (alpha, eta) ~ N(estimate, V) from the Tobit MLE's own sampling distribution (V = inverse observed
# information), push the draws through the SAME aggregation panels 2b/2d/2e use, and read off 95% CIs.
# Centered on the point estimate by construction. Runs inline (no MATLAB, no extra files / steps);
# saved as SI_Appendix_FigS9.pdf. All inputs are in scope via list2env(main_prep) above.

## Tobit negative log-likelihood - exact transcription of 4_Code/Matlab_OHI/C_lolik.m
nll <- function(par, shares, prices) {            # par = c(alpha, eta, log_sigma)
  alpha <- par[1]; eta <- par[2]; sigm <- max(exp(par[3]), 1e-5)
  mu <- 1 / (prices^((eta - 1)/eta) * ((1 - alpha)/alpha)^(1/eta) + 1)
  z0 <- shares == 0; z1 <- shares == 1; zi <- !z0 & !z1
  ll <- numeric(length(shares))
  if (any(z0)) ll[z0] <- log(pnorm(-mu[z0] / sigm))
  if (any(z1)) ll[z1] <- log(pmax(1e-8, 1 - pnorm((1 - mu[z1]) / sigm)))
  if (any(zi)) ll[zi] <- -0.5 * (log(2 * pi) + log(sigm^2) + ((shares[zi] - mu[zi]) / sigm)^2)
  -sum(ll)
}

## Compact central-difference gradient & Hessian
fd_grad <- function(f, x) {
  hs <- 1e-4 * pmax(abs(x), 1); g <- numeric(length(x))
  for (i in seq_along(x)) { xp <- xm <- x; xp[i] <- x[i] + hs[i]; xm[i] <- x[i] - hs[i]
    g[i] <- (f(xp) - f(xm)) / (2 * hs[i]) }
  g
}
fd_hessian <- function(f, x) {
  n <- length(x); hs <- 1e-4 * pmax(abs(x), 1); H <- matrix(0, n, n); f0 <- f(x)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    xp <- xm <- x; xp[i] <- x[i] + hs[i]; xm[i] <- x[i] - hs[i]
    H[i, i] <- (f(xp) - 2 * f0 + f(xm)) / hs[i]^2
    if (i < n) for (j in (i + 1):n) {
      e <- function(si, sj) { y <- x; y[i] <- x[i] + si * hs[i]; y[j] <- x[j] + sj * hs[j]; f(y) }
      H[i, j] <- H[j, i] <- (e(1, 1) - e(1, -1) - e(-1, 1) + e(-1, -1)) / (4 * hs[i] * hs[j])
    }
  }
  H
}

## Aggregation reused by every draw - identical math to panels 2b/2d/2e. No synthetic balancing:
## the main analysis uses the existing observations as-is, so every draw does too.
compute_fig2_summary <- function(estimates, scaffold) {
  alpha_total <- retrieve_alphas(estimates)   # na.omit inside drops nothing here (est_kr has no NA rows)
  eta_total   <- median(estimates$eta)        # median over the real block-level eta estimates
  df <- scaffold %>%
    mutate(eta_median = eta_total, alpha_median = alpha_total$alpha_median[match(goal, alpha_total$goal)]) %>%
    group_by(country) %>%
    mutate(adj_full  = calculate_OHI_score(alpha_median, goal_score, eta_median),
           adj_alpha = calculate_OHI_score(alpha_median, goal_score, rep(0, 10)),
           adj_eta   = calculate_OHI_score(rep(0.1, 10), goal_score, eta_median)) %>%
    ungroup() %>% distinct(country, .keep_all = TRUE)
  mb <- mean(df$base_OHI)
  list(summary = c(pct_alpha  = (mean(df$adj_alpha) - mb) / mb * 100,
                   pct_eta    = (mean(df$adj_eta)   - mb) / mb * 100,
                   pct_change = (mean(df$adj_full)  - mb) / mb * 100),
       alpha   = setNames(alpha_total$alpha_median, alpha_total$goal),  # per-goal weights (Panel 2a)
       eta     = eta_total)                                             # median substitutability (Panel 2c)
}

## Inputs
scaffold <- OHI_table %>% select(country, country_code, goal, goal_score, base_OHI)
est_kr <- ohi_estimates_online_raw %>%
  filter(paste(participant_code, task_number) %in%
         paste(main_sample_subject_selection$participant_code, main_sample_subject_selection$task_number)) %>%
  select(participant_code, task_number, task_name, alpha, eta, unipref)
dec <- data_decision_task_online %>%
  transmute(key = paste(participant_code, block_number), to_goal1_p, price_of_redist)
shares_by <- split(dec$to_goal1_p, dec$key); prices_by <- split(dec$price_of_redist, dec$key)

## Per-block covariance V = (alpha, eta) block of inverse observed information
nb <- nrow(est_kr); Vlist <- vector("list", nb); fixed <- logical(nb); grad_max <- rep(NA_real_, nb)
for (b in seq_len(nb)) {
  a_hat <- est_kr$alpha[b]; e_hat <- est_kr$eta[b]
  key <- paste(est_kr$participant_code[b], est_kr$task_number[b]); d_sh <- shares_by[[key]]; d_pr <- prices_by[[key]]
  if (isTRUE(est_kr$unipref[b] == 1) || a_hat <= 0 || a_hat >= 1 || e_hat <= 0 || is.null(d_sh)) { fixed[b] <- TRUE; next }
  f <- function(par) nll(par, d_sh, d_pr)
  ls_hat <- optimize(function(ls) f(c(a_hat, e_hat, ls)), interval = c(-12, 5))$minimum
  par_hat <- c(a_hat, e_hat, ls_hat)
  grad_max[b] <- max(abs(fd_grad(f, par_hat)[1:2]))
  V3 <- tryCatch(solve(fd_hessian(f, par_hat)), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(V3) || any(!is.finite(V3))) { fixed[b] <- TRUE; next }
  V <- V3[1:2, 1:2]
  if (V[1, 1] <= 0 || V[2, 2] <= 0 || (V[1, 1] * V[2, 2] - V[1, 2]^2) <= 0) { fixed[b] <- TRUE; next }
  Vlist[[b]] <- V
}

## Krinsky-Robb draws on (logit alpha, log eta), back-transformed; ill-conditioned blocks stay at point
S <- 1000; se_cap <- 5
.kr_rng <- if (exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())) get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv()) else NULL
set.seed(123)
alpha_draws <- matrix(est_kr$alpha, S, nb, byrow = TRUE); eta_draws <- matrix(est_kr$eta, S, nb, byrow = TRUE)
drawn <- logical(nb)
for (b in which(!fixed)) {
  a_hat <- est_kr$alpha[b]; e_hat <- est_kr$eta[b]; V <- Vlist[[b]]
  ja <- 1 / (a_hat * (1 - a_hat)); je <- 1 / e_hat
  Cg <- matrix(c(V[1, 1] * ja^2, V[1, 2] * ja * je, V[1, 2] * ja * je, V[2, 2] * je^2), 2, 2)
  if (sqrt(Cg[1, 1]) > se_cap || sqrt(Cg[2, 2]) > se_cap) next
  L <- tryCatch(chol(Cg), error = function(e) NULL); if (is.null(L)) next
  G <- matrix(rnorm(S * 2), S, 2) %*% L
  alpha_draws[, b] <- plogis(G[, 1] + qlogis(a_hat)); eta_draws[, b] <- exp(G[, 2] + log(e_hat))
  drawn[b] <- TRUE
}

## Propagate every draw (draw 0 = point estimate) through the panel aggregation. Each draw yields the
## aggregate %-changes (kr, panels 2b/2d/2e), the per-goal weights (Panel 2a) and the median
## substitutability (Panel 2c), so all three get the same Krinsky-Robb treatment in one pass.
panels      <- c("pct_alpha", "pct_eta", "pct_change")
goal_levels <- alpha_total_sample$goal
kr            <- matrix(NA_real_, S + 1, 3,                  dimnames = list(NULL, panels))
alpha_goal_kr <- matrix(NA_real_, S + 1, length(goal_levels), dimnames = list(NULL, goal_levels))
eta_med_kr    <- numeric(S + 1)
for (i in seq_len(S + 1)) {
  est_i <- est_kr
  if (i > 1) { est_i$alpha <- alpha_draws[i - 1, ]; est_i$eta <- eta_draws[i - 1, ] }  # i == 1 is the point estimate
  res <- compute_fig2_summary(est_i, scaffold)
  kr[i, ]            <- res$summary[panels]
  alpha_goal_kr[i, ] <- res$alpha[goal_levels]
  eta_med_kr[i]      <- res$eta
}
if (!is.null(.kr_rng)) assign(".Random.seed", .kr_rng, envir = globalenv())  # keep SI Appendix figures reproducible

## Panel point estimates (recomputed from OHI_table exactly as the panels do) + percentile CIs
.pe <- OHI_table %>%
  mutate(eta_median = eta_total_sample, alpha_median = alpha_total_sample$alpha_median[match(goal, alpha_total_sample$goal)]) %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  mutate(adj_full  = calculate_OHI_score(alpha_median, goal_score, eta_median),
         adj_alpha = calculate_OHI_score(alpha_median, goal_score, rep(0, 10)),
         adj_eta   = calculate_OHI_score(rep(0.1, 10), goal_score, eta_median)) %>%
  ungroup() %>% distinct(country, .keep_all = TRUE)
base_mean <- mean(.pe$base_OHI)
pts <- c(pct_alpha  = (mean(.pe$adj_alpha) - base_mean) / base_mean * 100,
         pct_eta    = (mean(.pe$adj_eta)   - base_mean) / base_mean * 100,
         pct_change = (mean(.pe$adj_full)  - base_mean) / base_mean * 100)
ci       <- apply(kr[-1, , drop = FALSE], 2, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)  # 2 x 3 (2.5%, 97.5%)
alpha_ci <- apply(alpha_goal_kr[-1, , drop = FALSE], 2, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)  # 2 x 10, cols = goals (Panel 2a)
eta_ci   <- quantile(eta_med_kr[-1], probs = c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)  # median-eta CI (Panel 2c)
eta_pt   <- eta_total_sample                                                # the value of the solid "Median Estimate" line in Panel 2c
a_pt     <- setNames(alpha_total_sample$alpha_median, alpha_total_sample$goal)[goal_levels]  # per-goal bar heights in Panel 2a

cat(sprintf("Krinsky-Robb: %d blocks, %d drawn (%.0f%%), %d fixed; max|grad(alpha,eta)| median=%.2g 90%%=%.2g\n",
            nb, sum(drawn), 100 * mean(drawn), sum(!drawn), median(grad_max, na.rm = TRUE), quantile(grad_max, 0.9, na.rm = TRUE)))
for (p in panels)     cat(sprintf("  %-11s point %+6.2f%%  95%% CI [%+6.2f%%, %+6.2f%%]\n", p, pts[p], ci[1, p], ci[2, p]))
for (g in goal_levels) cat(sprintf("  alpha[%-2s]   point %.3f   95%% CI [%.3f, %.3f]\n", g, a_pt[g], alpha_ci[1, g], alpha_ci[2, g]))
cat(sprintf("  %-11s point %6.2f    95%% CI [%6.2f, %6.2f]\n", "eta_median", eta_pt, eta_ci[1], eta_ci[2]))
stopifnot(abs(kr[1, "pct_change"] - pts["pct_change"]) < 1e-6)   # draw 0 reproduces the headline
if (!(ci[1, "pct_change"] <= pts["pct_change"] && pts["pct_change"] <= ci[2, "pct_change"]))
  warning("Krinsky-Robb 95% CI for Panel 2e does not bracket the point estimate.")
if (abs(eta_med_kr[1] - eta_pt) > 1e-6)
  warning("Krinsky-Robb: draw 0 median eta does not match the Panel 2c line (eta_total_sample).")
# Real invariant: draw 0 must reproduce the Panel 2a bar heights, i.e. retrieve_alphas() is applied to
# the draws exactly as to the point estimate. This guards against an actual transform/pipeline bug.
stopifnot(max(abs(alpha_goal_kr[1, ] - a_pt), na.rm = TRUE) < 1e-6)
if (!(eta_ci[1] <= eta_pt && eta_pt <= eta_ci[2]))
  warning("Krinsky-Robb 95% CI for the Panel 2c eta does not bracket the point estimate.")
# Per-goal alpha brackets are NOT asserted: retrieve_alphas() is a nonlinear normalized aggregator
# (per-pair median -> Hovanov geometric mean -> renormalize to sum 1), so the percentile interval is
# bias-shifted for the extreme weights (e.g. TR at the floor, CW at the ceiling) and need not contain
# the point. This is expected, not a transform error - draw 0 above reproduces every bar; the point
# estimate is retained as the reported weight.

## Build a CI-overlay version of Figure 2: copy the unchanged main panels and place the CI brackets
## directly under each headline number (the main figure objects are never modified - R copy-on-
## modify). Shared by this chunk (Krinsky-Robb CIs -> SI_Appendix_FigS9.pdf) and the decision-block
## bootstrap chunk below (-> SI_Appendix_FigS10.pdf), which differ only in the CI values and the
## output file.
build_fig2_ci_figure <- function(ci, alpha_ci, eta_ci, pts, eta_pt, filename) {
  ci_lab  <- function(p, unit = "%") sprintf("[%+.1f%s, %+.1f%s]", ci[1, p], unit, ci[2, p], unit)

  # Panel 2a: one rotated weighting-CI bracket inside each bar, in the same goal order/levels as the bars
  goal_order  <- alpha_total_sample %>% arrange(desc(alpha_median)) %>% pull(goal)
  alpha_ci_df <- tibble::tibble(goal   = factor(goal_order, levels = goal_order),
                                ci_lab = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", alpha_ci[1, goal_order], alpha_ci[2, goal_order]))
  panel_fig2_a_ci <- main_panels$panel_fig2_a +
    geom_text(data = alpha_ci_df, aes(x = goal, y = 0.025, label = ci_lab),
              angle = 90, hjust = 0.35, vjust = -0.5, size = 5 / .pt, inherit.aes = FALSE)

  # Sensitivity-analysis (CI) panel only: TR's bar is too narrow to hold both its point
  # estimate and the rotated CI bracket. Lift TR's point estimate above the bar (as already
  # done for the above-equal-weighting goals); the main figure and all other goals are unchanged.
  pe_idx <- which(vapply(panel_fig2_a_ci$layers,
                         function(l) inherits(l$geom, "GeomText") && !is.null(l$mapping$vjust),
                         logical(1)))
  stopifnot(length(pe_idx) == 1L)   # the point-estimate label layer must be uniquely identified
  panel_fig2_a_ci$layers[[pe_idx]]$mapping$vjust <-
    rlang::quo(ifelse(goal == "TR" | alpha_median >= 0.1, -0.5, 1.5))

  # Panel 2c: show the median-eta value (previously unlabelled) and its CI next to the "Median Estimate" line
  panel_fig2_c_ci <- main_panels$panel_fig2_c +
    annotate("text", x = eta_pt + 0.18, y = 0.47,
             label = sprintf("%.2f  [%.2f, %.2f]", eta_pt, eta_ci[1], eta_ci[2]),
             angle = -90, hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 6 / .pt, colour = "#08519c")

  # Sensitivity-analysis (CI) panel only: split the baked-in "-2% / (p<0.001)" annotation
  # so the CI bracket can sit between the percent change (top) and the p-value (bottom), and
  # shift the whole text block slightly left so the wide CI bracket clears the box plot. The
  # main figure's panel_fig2_b (with the combined annotation) is left untouched.
  # The annotation is the only layer carrying a one-row data frame; everything else is the
  # (multi-row) point/box/violin data. We reuse its "(p<0.001)" line verbatim and take the headline
  # percent from pts["pct_alpha"] -- the identical mean %-change the main figure shows, recomputed in
  # this chunk (so no cross-chunk object is needed) -- formatted to one decimal.
  b_lab_idx <- which(vapply(main_panels$panel_fig2_b$layers,
                            function(l) is.data.frame(l$data) && nrow(l$data) == 1L,
                            logical(1)))
  stopifnot(length(b_lab_idx) == 1L)   # the percent/p-value label layer must be uniquely identified
  b_lab_layer <- main_panels$panel_fig2_b$layers[[b_lab_idx]]
  b_lab_txt   <- if (!is.null(b_lab_layer$aes_params$label)) b_lab_layer$aes_params$label else b_lab_layer$data$label
  b_lab_parts <- strsplit(as.character(b_lab_txt), "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]   # c("-2%", "(p<0.001)")
  panel_fig2_b_ci <- main_panels$panel_fig2_b
  panel_fig2_b_ci$layers[[b_lab_idx]] <- NULL
  panel_fig2_b_ci <- panel_fig2_b_ci +
    annotate("text", x = 2.515, y = 72, label = sprintf("%.1f%%", pts["pct_alpha"]), size = 6 / .pt) +
    annotate("text", x = 2.515, y = 65, label = ci_lab("pct_alpha", unit = ""), size = 6 / .pt) +
    annotate("text", x = 2.515, y = 58, label = b_lab_parts[2], size = 6 / .pt)
  # Same treatment as panel b: split the baked-in "-N% / (p<0.001)" annotation so the CI bracket
  # sits between the percent change (top) and the p-value (bottom). d's base block is 10 units
  # lower than b's, so the y-anchors are b's minus 10. The one-row data frame uniquely identifies
  # the annotation layer; reuse its "(p<0.001)" line and take the headline percent from
  # pts["pct_eta"] (the identical mean %-change the main figure shows, recomputed in this chunk),
  # formatted to one decimal.
  d_lab_idx <- which(vapply(main_panels$panel_fig2_d$layers,
                            function(l) is.data.frame(l$data) && nrow(l$data) == 1L,
                            logical(1)))
  stopifnot(length(d_lab_idx) == 1L)   # the percent/p-value label layer must be uniquely identified
  d_lab_layer <- main_panels$panel_fig2_d$layers[[d_lab_idx]]
  d_lab_txt   <- if (!is.null(d_lab_layer$aes_params$label)) d_lab_layer$aes_params$label else d_lab_layer$data$label
  d_lab_parts <- strsplit(as.character(d_lab_txt), "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]   # c("-N%", "(p<0.001)")
  panel_fig2_d_ci <- main_panels$panel_fig2_d
  panel_fig2_d_ci$layers[[d_lab_idx]] <- NULL
  panel_fig2_d_ci <- panel_fig2_d_ci +
    annotate("text", x = 2.515, y = 62, label = sprintf("%.1f%%", pts["pct_eta"]), size = 6 / .pt) +
    annotate("text", x = 2.515, y = 55, label = ci_lab("pct_eta", unit = ""), size = 6 / .pt) +
    annotate("text", x = 2.515, y = 48, label = d_lab_parts[2], size = 6 / .pt)
  # Panel e: the headline %-change is baked into panel_fig2_e as an integer-rounded geom_text (the
  # only text layer whose label references both adjusted_OHI and base_OHI). Drop it on the CI copy
  # and redraw with one decimal, sourcing the value from pts["pct_change"] (the identical mean
  # %-change, recomputed in this chunk); the main figure's panel_fig2_e is untouched (R copy-on-modify).
  e_lab_idx <- which(vapply(main_panels$panel_fig2_e$layers,
                            function(l) inherits(l$geom, "GeomText") && !is.null(l$mapping$label) &&
                                        grepl("adjusted_OHI", rlang::quo_text(l$mapping$label), fixed = TRUE) &&
                                        grepl("base_OHI",     rlang::quo_text(l$mapping$label), fixed = TRUE),
                            logical(1)))
  stopifnot(length(e_lab_idx) == 1L)   # the headline %-change label layer must be uniquely identified
  panel_fig2_e_ci <- main_panels$panel_fig2_e
  panel_fig2_e_ci$layers[[e_lab_idx]] <- NULL
  panel_fig2_e_ci <- panel_fig2_e_ci +
    annotate("text", x = 63, y = 0.096, vjust = 0, hjust = 0, size = 7 / .pt,
             label = sprintf("%.1f%%", pts["pct_change"])) +
    annotate("text", x = 60, y = 0.091, label = ci_lab("pct_change", unit = ""), size = 7 / .pt, hjust = 0)

  panel_fig2_CI <- ggdraw() +
    draw_plot(panel_fig2_a_ci,          x = 0,    y = 0.69, width = 0.5,  height = 0.3,  scale = 1) +
    draw_plot(panel_fig2_b_ci,          x = 0.52, y = 0.72, width = 0.48, height = 0.27, scale = 1) +
    draw_plot(panel_fig2_c_ci,          x = 0.02, y = 0.42, width = 0.48, height = 0.28, scale = 1) +
    draw_plot(panel_fig2_d_ci,          x = 0.52, y = 0.43, width = 0.48, height = 0.27, scale = 1) +
    draw_plot(panel_fig2_e_ci,          x = 0.03, y = 0,    width = 0.9,  height = 0.41, scale = 1) +
    draw_plot_label(c("a", "b", "c", "d", "e"), x = c(0, 0.5, 0, 0.5, 0), y = c(1, 1, 0.73, 0.73, 0.44), size = 10)

  save_plot(filename = here::here("2_Graphs", filename),
            plot = panel_fig2_CI, base_width = 7.2, base_height = 6.69)
}

build_fig2_ci_figure(ci, alpha_ci, eta_ci, pts, eta_pt, "SI_Appendix_FigS9.pdf")
```

```{r}
# ---- Figure 2 with decision-block bootstrap confidence intervals (SAMPLING-uncertainty SENSITIVITY) ----
# Companion to the Krinsky-Robb figure (SI_Appendix_FigS9.pdf) above, capturing a DIFFERENT source of
# uncertainty. Krinsky-Robb perturbs each block's (alpha, eta) within its own Tobit-MLE sampling
# distribution (within-block parameter/estimation uncertainty). Here we instead resample the decision
# blocks themselves: we draw B = 1000 new samples of the main-sample blocks (rows of est_kr, each
# carrying its estimated point (alpha, eta)) with replacement and the SAME sample size, push every
# resample through the SAME aggregation panels 2a/2b/2c/2d/2e use (compute_fig2_summary), and read off
# the central 95% (2.5/97.5 percentiles) for each reported panel quantity. This captures between-block
# sampling uncertainty. Runs inline; reuses est_kr, scaffold, compute_fig2_summary, the reported
# panel quantities (panels, goal_levels), the point estimates (pts, eta_pt, a_pt) and the overlay
# function build_fig2_ci_figure() from the Krinsky-Robb chunk above; saved as SI_Appendix_FigS10.pdf.

## Decision-block bootstrap: resample est_kr rows (blocks) with replacement, same n, B times.
B <- 1000; nb_boot <- nrow(est_kr)
.boot_rng <- if (exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())) get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv()) else NULL
set.seed(123)
boot_summary <- matrix(NA_real_, B, length(panels),      dimnames = list(NULL, panels))
boot_alpha   <- matrix(NA_real_, B, length(goal_levels), dimnames = list(NULL, goal_levels))
boot_eta     <- numeric(B)
for (b in seq_len(B)) {
  est_b <- est_kr[sample.int(nb_boot, nb_boot, replace = TRUE), , drop = FALSE]
  res   <- compute_fig2_summary(est_b, scaffold)
  boot_summary[b, ] <- res$summary[panels]
  boot_alpha[b, ]   <- res$alpha[goal_levels]
  boot_eta[b]       <- res$eta
}
if (!is.null(.boot_rng)) assign(".Random.seed", .boot_rng, envir = globalenv())  # keep SI Appendix figures reproducible

## Central 95% percentile CIs over the 1000 resamples (the "central 95% of observations").
ci       <- apply(boot_summary, 2, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)  # 2 x 3 (2.5%, 97.5%)
alpha_ci <- apply(boot_alpha,   2, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)  # 2 x 10, cols = goals (Panel 2a)
eta_ci   <- quantile(boot_eta,  probs = c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)               # median-eta CI (Panel 2c)

cat(sprintf("Decision-block bootstrap: B = %d resamples, n = %d blocks (with replacement)\n", B, nb_boot))
for (p in panels)      cat(sprintf("  %-11s point %+6.2f%%  95%% CI [%+6.2f%%, %+6.2f%%]\n", p, pts[p], ci[1, p], ci[2, p]))
for (g in goal_levels) cat(sprintf("  alpha[%-2s]   point %.3f   95%% CI [%.3f, %.3f]\n", g, a_pt[g], alpha_ci[1, g], alpha_ci[2, g]))
cat(sprintf("  %-11s point %6.2f    95%% CI [%6.2f, %6.2f]\n", "eta_median", eta_pt, eta_ci[1], eta_ci[2]))
# A bootstrap percentile CI need not bracket the point estimate (the resampling distribution can be
# skewed), so - unlike the Krinsky-Robb chunk - no "brackets the point" invariant is asserted here.
stopifnot(all(is.finite(pts)), all(is.finite(ci)), all(is.finite(alpha_ci)), all(is.finite(eta_ci)))  # reported values are well-defined

build_fig2_ci_figure(ci, alpha_ci, eta_ci, pts, eta_pt, "SI_Appendix_FigS10.pdf")
```

```{r}
# ---- SI Appendix Fig. S11: Fig 2 panels d & e at non-median eta percentiles (SENSITIVITY) ----
# A simpler, assumption-light companion to the Krinsky-Robb chunk above. The main Figure 2 sets every
# country's substitutability to the MEDIAN (50th percentile) of the main-sample eta estimates. Here we
# rebuild panels d and e at the 25th, 40th, 60th and 75th percentiles of the SAME eta pool, holding
# alpha at the main-analysis values throughout (alpha is not decisive, so only eta varies). The d/e
# annotations (-% change, means) are the original data-driven code and so update per percentile.
#
# Everything is sourced from `main_prep` (the untouched main sample) and wrapped in local(), so the
# main figure and every downstream output are unaffected. Panel d uses jitter(); we set.seed(123) for
# reproducibility and restore the prior RNG state on exit so later figures stay bit-identical.
local({
  OHI_table           <- main_prep$OHI_table
  alpha_total_sample  <- main_prep$alpha_total_sample
  calculate_OHI_score <- main_prep$calculate_OHI_score
  eta_pool            <- main_prep$ohi_estimates_online$eta   # na.omit'd at import; 50th pct == main median

  old_seed <- if (exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())) get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv()) else NULL
  on.exit(if (!is.null(old_seed)) assign(".Random.seed", old_seed, envir = globalenv()), add = TRUE)

  pct_labels <- c("25th", "40th", "60th", "75th")
  eta_probs  <- c(0.25, 0.40, 0.60, 0.75)
  eta_values <- quantile(eta_pool, probs = eta_probs, na.rm = TRUE)

  # Build panels d (substitutability only, equal weights) and e (alpha + eta) for one eta value.
  # Faithful copy of the main-figure panel d/e code with the median eta swapped for `eta_value`;
  # alpha is kept at the main per-goal medians (rep(0.1, 10) for d, alpha_median for e).
  build_fig2_de_for_eta <- function(eta_value) {
    ## Panel d - shift in OHI from substitutability only
    panel_fig2_d_data <- OHI_table %>%
        mutate(eta_median = eta_value) %>%
        mutate(alpha_median = alpha_total_sample$alpha_median[match(goal, alpha_total_sample$goal)]) %>%
        group_by(country) %>%
        mutate(adjusted_OHI_etaonly = calculate_OHI_score(rep(0.1, 10), goal_score, eta_median)) %>%
        ungroup()

    panel_fig2_d_data_long <- panel_fig2_d_data %>%
      select(country, base_OHI, adjusted_OHI_etaonly) %>%
      distinct(country, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
      pivot_longer(cols = c("base_OHI", "adjusted_OHI_etaonly"), names_to = "name", values_to = "value")

    panel_fig2_d_data_long$x <- ifelse(panel_fig2_d_data_long$name == "base_OHI", 1, 2)
    panel_fig2_d_data_long$jittered_x <- jitter(panel_fig2_d_data_long$x, .1)

    panel_fig2_d_meantest <- panel_fig2_d_data_long %>%
        summarize(
                meanscore_before = mean(value[x == 1], na.rm = TRUE),
                meanscore_after = mean(value[x == 2], na.rm = TRUE),
                p_value = t.test(value[x == 1], value[x == 2], paired = TRUE)$p.value,
                mean_diff = (meanscore_after - meanscore_before) / meanscore_before * 100,
                )

    panel_fig2_d <- ggplot(data = panel_fig2_d_data_long, aes(y = value)) +
        geom_point(data = panel_fig2_d_data_long %>% filter(name == "base_OHI"), aes(x = jittered_x, color = "Baseline"), size = 0.3, alpha = .5) +
        geom_point(data = panel_fig2_d_data_long %>% filter(name == "adjusted_OHI_etaonly"), aes(x = jittered_x, color = "Substitutability-Adjusted"), size = 0.3, alpha = .5) +
        geom_line(aes(x = jittered_x, group = country), color = 'lightgray', alpha = .5, linewidth = 0.1) +
        geom_half_boxplot(
            data = panel_fig2_d_data_long %>% filter(name == "base_OHI"), aes(x = x, y = value), position = position_nudge(x = 1.25),
            side = "r", outlier.shape = NA, center = TRUE, errorbar.draw = TRUE, width = .07,
            alpha = .5, size = 0.2, fill = "#D55E00") +
        geom_half_boxplot(
            data = panel_fig2_d_data_long %>% filter(name == "adjusted_OHI_etaonly"), aes(x = x, y = value), position = position_nudge(x = .3),
            side = "r", outlier.shape = NA, center = TRUE, errorbar.draw = TRUE, width = .07,
            alpha = .5, size = 0.2, fill = "#08519c") +
        geom_half_violin(
            data = panel_fig2_d_data_long %>% filter(name == "adjusted_OHI_etaonly"), aes(x = x, y = value), position = position_nudge(x = .05),
            side = "r", alpha = .5, trim = TRUE, size = 0.2, adjust = 0.6, width = 0.3, fill = "#08519c") +
        geom_half_violin(
            data = panel_fig2_d_data_long %>% filter(name == "base_OHI"), aes(x = x, y = value), position = position_nudge(x = 1.05),
            side = "r", alpha = .5, trim = TRUE, size = 0.2, adjust = 0.6, width = 0.3, fill = "#D55E00") +
        annotate("text", x = 2.50, y = 60, label = paste(paste0(round(panel_fig2_d_meantest$mean_diff, 0), "%"),
                                                          paste0("(", ifelse(panel_fig2_d_meantest$p_value < 0.001, "p<0.001", sprintf("p=%.3f", panel_fig2_d_meantest$p_value)), ")"),
                                                          sep = "\n"), size = 7 / .pt) +
        scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 2), labels = c("Baseline country scores", 'Substitutability-adjusted country scores')) +
        scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(seq(0, 95, 10))) +
        scale_color_manual(values = c("Baseline" = "#D55E00", "Substitutability-Adjusted" = "#08519c")) +
        guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 1))) +
        xlab("") + ylab("OHI score") +
        theme_classic() +
        coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.9, 2.6), ylim = c(0, 90)) +
        theme(
            axis.title = element_text(size = 7),
            axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
            axis.text.y = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = .5),
            axis.line.x = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.3),
            axis.line.y = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.3),
            legend.position = "none",
            legend.title = element_blank(),
            legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
            plot.margin = margin(t = 2, r = 2, b = 2, l = 2, unit = "pt")
        )

    ## Panel e - distribution of OHI scores before and after total adjustment
    panel_fig2_e_data <- OHI_table %>%
        mutate(eta_median = eta_value) %>%
        mutate(alpha_median = alpha_total_sample$alpha_median[match(goal, alpha_total_sample$goal)])

    panel_fig2_e_data <- panel_fig2_e_data %>%
        group_by(country) %>%
        mutate(adjusted_OHI = calculate_OHI_score(alpha_median, goal_score, eta_median)) %>%
        ungroup() %>%
        distinct(country, .keep_all = TRUE)

    panel_fig2_e <- ggplot() +
        geom_density(data = panel_fig2_e_data, aes(x = base_OHI), color = "#D55E00", fill = "#D55E00", alpha = 0.4) +
        geom_density(data = panel_fig2_e_data, aes(x = adjusted_OHI), color = "#009E73", fill = "#009E73", alpha = 0.4) +
        geom_segment(
            data = panel_fig2_e_data,
            aes(x = mean(base_OHI), xend = mean(base_OHI), y = 0, yend = 0.1, color = "Baseline", linetype = "Mean"),
            linewidth = 0.3
        ) +
        geom_text(
            data = panel_fig2_e_data,
            aes(x = mean(base_OHI), y = 0.1, label = round(mean(base_OHI), 0)), vjust = -0.5, hjust = 0.5, size = 7 / .pt, check_overlap = TRUE
        ) +
        geom_segment(
            data = panel_fig2_e_data,
            aes(x = mean(adjusted_OHI), xend = mean(adjusted_OHI), y = 0, yend = 0.1, color = "Adjusted", linetype = "Mean"),
            linewidth = 0.3
        ) +
        geom_text(
            data = panel_fig2_e_data,
            aes(x = mean(adjusted_OHI), y = 0.1, label = round(mean(adjusted_OHI), 0)), vjust = -0.5, hjust = 0.7, size = 7 / .pt, check_overlap = TRUE
        ) +
        geom_segment(
            data = panel_fig2_e_data,
            aes(x = mean(adjusted_OHI), xend = mean(base_OHI), y = 0.095, yend = 0.095),
            arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.1, "cm"), ends = "first", type = "open", angle = 30),
            linewidth = 0.2
        ) +
        geom_text(
            data = panel_fig2_e_data,
            aes(x = 63, y = 0.096, label = paste0(round((1 - mean(panel_fig2_e_data$adjusted_OHI) / mean(panel_fig2_e_data$base_OHI)) * -100), "%")), vjust = 0, hjust = 0, size = 7 / .pt, check_overlap = TRUE
        ) +
        labs(x = "OHI score", y = "Density") +
        scale_x_continuous(limit = c(0, 100), expand = c(0, 0), breaks = seq(0, 100, 10)) +
        scale_y_continuous(limit = c(0, 0.11), expand = c(0, 0)) +
        # Compact labels (the full "Officially reported.../Recalculated..." wording from the main
        # Figure 2 would overlap the densities when repeated across four reduced-size rows; it belongs
        # in this figure's caption). Baseline vs adjusted are otherwise identical to the main panel e.
        scale_color_manual(breaks = c("Baseline", "Adjusted"), values = c("Baseline" = "#D55E00", "Adjusted" = "#009E73"),
                           labels = c("Baseline", "Adjusted")) +
        scale_linetype_manual(breaks = c("Median", "Mean"), values = c("Median" = "solid", "Mean" = "dashed")) +
        theme_basic +
        theme(
            legend.position = "inside",
            legend.position.inside = c(0.02, 0.98),
            legend.justification.inside = c(0, 1),
            legend.background = element_blank(),
            legend.title = element_blank(),
            legend.text = element_text(size = 6),
            legend.spacing.x = unit(0, "mm"),
            legend.spacing.y = unit(0, "mm"),
            legend.key.height = unit(0.9, "lines"),
            legend.key.width = unit(0.8, "lines"),
            axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, vjust = 6, size = 7),
            axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 7),
            plot.margin = unit(c(0.05, 0.35, 0, 0), "cm"),
            axis.title.x = element_text(size = 7, vjust = 6),  # nudge title up within its slot (panel height + mean labels unchanged)
            axis.title.y = element_text(size = 7),
            panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
            axis.ticks.length = unit(0.1, "cm"),
            axis.ticks.x = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3),
            axis.ticks.y = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3),
            axis.line.x = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.3),
            axis.line.y = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.3)
        )

    list(d = panel_fig2_d, e = panel_fig2_e)
  }

  # One row: a rotated bold percentile label down the left margin, then panels d and e.
  make_titled_row <- function(panels, title_expr) {
    body <- cowplot::plot_grid(panels$d, panels$e, ncol = 2, rel_widths = c(0.44, 0.56))
    lab  <- cowplot::ggdraw() +
            cowplot::draw_label(title_expr, fontface = "bold", size = 8, angle = 90, x = 0.5, y = 0.5)
    cowplot::plot_grid(lab, body, ncol = 2, rel_widths = c(0.045, 1))
  }

  set.seed(123)   # panel d uses jitter(); fix it so this sensitivity figure is reproducible
  rows <- lapply(seq_along(eta_values), function(i) {
    title_expr <- latex2exp::TeX(sprintf("$\\eta$ at %s percentile $= %.2f$", pct_labels[i], eta_values[i]))
    make_titled_row(build_fig2_de_for_eta(eta_values[i]), title_expr)
  })

  extdata_fig8 <- cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = rows, ncol = 1)

  save_plot(filename = here::here("2_Graphs", "SI_Appendix_FigS11.pdf"),
            plot = extdata_fig8, base_width = 7.2, base_height = 6.69)
})
```

```{r}
# Obtain the estimates for the goal pairs in both orderings

                              y = grid_combinations,
                              by = c("task_name" = "goal_pair_reverse"))

# We reverse the estimates of the second table
goal_estimates2 %<>%
  mutate(alpha = 1 - alpha) %>%
  select(-task_name) %>%
  rename(task_name = goal_pair)

# And append them to the first table
df <- rbind(goal_estimates1, goal_estimates2)

median_estimates <- df %>%
    tidyr::separate_wider_delim(task_name, delim = "-", names = c("goal1", "goal2")) %>%
    group_by(goal1, goal2) %>%
    summarize(median_alpha = round(median(alpha, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
            median_eta = round(median(eta, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
            datapoints = n()) %>%
    rbind( # Manually add missing goal pairs (for visual completeness)
        tibble(goal1 = "AO",

               median_eta = NA,

               goal2 = "TR",
               median_alpha = NA,
               median_eta = NA,
               datapoints = NA)
```

```{r}
#### SI Appendix Fig. S4a: OHI score distribution baseline vs. only Eta adjustment for all 220 countries
# Obtain a table with the total country scores in 2022
base_OHI_2022_full <- ohi_scores %>% 
  filter(scenario == 2022,
         goal == "Index",
         dimension == "score") %>%
  select(region_name, value) %>%
  filter(region_name != "Global average")

# Obtain a table with all OHI scores by goal and country in 2022
OHI_scores_2022_goallevel_full <- ohi_scores %>%
    filter(scenario == 2022,
         goal %in% goal_names$goal_code_eng,
         dimension == "score") %>%
         arrange(goal) %>%
  filter(region_name != "Global average")

# Manually add the missing data on TR for Japan & Australia (from OHI website)
OHI_scores_2022_goallevel_full <- OHI_scores_2022_goallevel_full %>%
    mutate(value = ifelse(region_name %in% c("Japan", "Australia") & goal == "TR", 100, value))

# Join the alpha and eta values with the OHI scores
OHI_table_full <- OHI_scores_2022_goallevel_full %>%
    full_join( # Join OHI scores with alpha values
        y = alpha_allcountries_goallevel,
        by = c('goal', 'region_name')) %>%
        select(goal, region_name, value, alpha_median) %>%
        mutate(country_code = country_abrv$country_abrv[match(region_name, country_abrv$region_name)]) %>%
        rename(country=region_name, score=value) %>%
    full_join( # Join OHI scores with eta values
        y = eta_per_country[, c('Country', 'Median')],
        join_by(country_code == Country)) %>%
        rename(eta_median = Median) %>%
  filter(country != "All")

# All countries get the overall eta value and 1/n alpha values
OHI_table_full <- OHI_table_full %>%
    filter(!is.na(score)) %>%
    mutate(eta_median = eta_total_sample) %>%
    group_by(country) %>%
    mutate(alpha_median = 1 / n()) %>%
    ungroup()

# Calculate adjusted OHI scores
OHI_table_full <- OHI_table_full %>%
    group_by(country) %>%
    mutate(adjusted_OHI = calculate_OHI_score(alpha_median, score, eta_median)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    left_join(
        y = base_OHI_2022_full,
        by = c("country" = "region_name")) %>%
    rename(base_OHI = value,
        goal_score = score)

# Save as plot data (one row per country, mirroring main Fig. 2e / panel d so the kernel
# density weights every country equally instead of by its number of reported goals)
extdata_fig4_a_data <- OHI_table_full %>%
    distinct(country, .keep_all = TRUE)

extdata_fig4_a <- plot_ohi_density_panel(extdata_fig4_a_data,
    "All 220 OHI countries (substitutability−adjustment only)")

# For Text: Use a Welch two-sample t-test to compare means of base_OHI and adjusted_OHI
t.test(extdata_fig4_a_data$base_OHI, extdata_fig4_a_data$adjusted_OHI, var.equal = FALSE)

#### SI Appendix Fig. S4b: Post-Covid Sensitivity Analysis of OHI Score Distributions
## Prepare OHI Table for 2024
# Obtain a table with the total country scores in 2024
base_OHI_2024 <- ohi_scores %>% 
  filter(scenario == 2024,
         goal == "Index",
         dimension == "score") %>%
  filter(!is.na(value)) %>% 
  select(region_name, value) %>%
  mutate(rank = rank(-value, ties.method = "min"))

# Obtain a table with all OHI scores by goal and country in 2024
OHI_scores_2024_goallevel <- ohi_scores %>%
    filter(scenario == 2024,
         goal %in% goal_names$goal_code_eng,
         dimension == "score") %>%
         arrange(goal) 

# Throw out all countries that have some missing goal score
OHI_scores_2024_goallevel <- OHI_scores_2024_goallevel %>%
       group_by(region_name) %>%
       filter(!any(is.na(value))) %>%
       ungroup()

# Replace german goal names with english goal abbreviations and transform to long format
alpha_allcountries_goallevel <- alpha_per_country %>% 
    mutate(goal = goal_names$goal_code_eng[match(goal, goal_names$goal_name)]) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = -goal, names_to = "region_name", values_to = "alpha_median") %>%
    mutate(alpha_median = as.numeric(alpha_median)) %>%
    mutate(region_name = country_abrv$region_name[match(region_name, country_abrv$country_abrv)])

# Join the alpha and eta values with the OHI scores
OHI_table_2024 <- OHI_scores_2024_goallevel %>%
    full_join( # Join OHI scores with alpha values
        y = alpha_allcountries_goallevel,
        by = c('goal', 'region_name')) %>%
        select(goal, region_name, value, alpha_median) %>%
        mutate(country_code = country_abrv$country_abrv[match(region_name, country_abrv$region_name)]) %>%
        rename(country=region_name, score=value) %>%
    full_join( # Join OHI scores with eta values (per-country medians for surveyed countries; others get the overall median below)
        y = eta_per_country[, c('Country', 'Median')],
        join_by(country_code == Country)) %>%
        rename(eta_median = Median)

# All Countries get overall median & eta values
OHI_table_2024 <- OHI_table_2024 %>%
    mutate(eta_median = eta_total_sample,
          alpha_median = alpha_total_sample$alpha_median[match(goal, alpha_total_sample$goal)])

# Calculate adjusted OHI scores
OHI_table_2024 <- OHI_table_2024 %>%
    group_by(country) %>%
    mutate(adjusted_OHI = calculate_OHI_score(alpha_median, score, eta_median)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(rank = dense_rank(adjusted_OHI))

# Add base OHI scores and rename columns
OHI_table_2024 <- OHI_table_2024 %>%
    left_join(
        y = base_OHI_2024,
        by = c("country" = "region_name")) %>%
    select(-c(rank.x, rank.y)) %>% # Drop ranks as these are recalculated in the next step
    rename(base_OHI = value,
        goal_score = score)

# Determine ranks for each country (workaround as ties could come from both duplicate rows and equal country scores)
OHI_table_2024_ranks <- OHI_table_2024 %>%
    filter(country != "Global average") %>% # Don't rank the global average
    distinct(country, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(base_rank = rank(-base_OHI, ties.method = "min")) %>%
    mutate(adjusted_rank = rank(-adjusted_OHI, ties.method = "min")) %>%
    select(country, base_rank, adjusted_rank)

# Join ranks with OHI table
OHI_table_2024 <- OHI_table_2024 %>%
    left_join(
        y = OHI_table_2024_ranks,
        by = c("country")) %>%
    relocate(c("country_code", "country", "goal", "goal_score", "alpha_median", "eta_median", "base_OHI", "adjusted_OHI", "base_rank", "adjusted_rank")) %>%
    arrange(country) %>%
    filter(is.na(country_code)|country_code!="All") # Remove 'All' row (workaround as filter usually excludes all NA values, which we don't want here)

# Save as plot data (one row per country, mirroring main Fig. 2e / panel d)
extdata_fig4_b_data <- OHI_table_2024 %>%
    filter(!is.na(goal_score)) %>% # Throws out Australia and Japan as they have no data for TR in 2024
    distinct(country, .keep_all = TRUE)

extdata_fig4_b <- plot_ohi_density_panel(extdata_fig4_b_data,
    "Post-COVID robustness check (2024 OHI scores)", pct_x = 50)

#### SI Appendix Fig. S4c: OHI score distribution by Coastal Affinity

# Merge block-level estimates with the survey data and split participants by coastal affinity
# (more than 10 days per year spent at the coast)
ohi_estimates_online_withsurvey <- ohi_estimates_online %>%
    inner_join(
        y = survey_data[ , c("participant_code", "gender", "age", "siblings", "number_moves", "days_at_sea", "ocean_health_importance", "session_label")],
        by = c("participant_code"),
        multiple = "any")

fig_Xe_data <- ohi_estimates_online_withsurvey %>%
    mutate(coast_native = ifelse(days_at_sea > 10, 1, 0))

# For text: Median alpha and eta by coastal affinity
fig_Xe_data %>%
    group_by(coast_native) %>%
    summarize(
        median_eta = median(eta, na.rm = TRUE),
        median_alpha = median(alpha, na.rm = TRUE),
    )

# For text: Perform Wilcoxon rank sum test for eta
wilcox.test(eta ~ coast_native, data = fig_Xe_data)

# For text: Median eta for coastal natives and non-coastal natives
fig_Xe_data %>%
    filter(coast_native == 1) %>%
    summarize(median_eta = median(eta, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    pull(median_eta)

fig_Xe_data %>%
    filter(coast_native == 0) %>%
    summarize(median_eta = median(eta, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    pull(median_eta)

# For text: Number of participants classified as coast native vs. not
fig_Xe_data %>%
    group_by(coast_native) %>%
    summarize(n_participants = n_distinct(participant_code))

extdata_fig4_c_data <- retrieve_alphas(fig_Xe_data[fig_Xe_data$coast_native == 0, ]) %>%
    rename(median_non_coastnative = alpha_median) %>%
    left_join(
        y = retrieve_alphas(fig_Xe_data[fig_Xe_data$coast_native == 1, ]) %>%
            rename(median_coastnative = alpha_median),
        by = "goal"
    ) %>% bind_rows(
        tibble(
            goal = "Eta",
            median_non_coastnative = fig_Xe_data %>%
                filter(coast_native == 0) %>%
                summarize(median_eta = median(eta, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
                pull(median_eta),
            median_coastnative = fig_Xe_data %>%
                filter(coast_native == 1) %>%
                summarize(median_eta = median(eta, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
                pull(median_eta)
        )
    ) %>%
    rename(goal_or_eta = goal)

# All Countries get overall median & eta values
extdata_fig4_c_data <- OHI_table %>%
    left_join(y = extdata_fig4_c_data,
              by = c("goal" = "goal_or_eta")) %>%
    mutate(eta_median_noncoastal = extdata_fig4_c_data$median_non_coastnative[match("Eta", extdata_fig4_c_data$goal_or_eta)],
           eta_median_coastal = extdata_fig4_c_data$median_coastnative[match("Eta", extdata_fig4_c_data$goal_or_eta)]) %>%
    rename(alpha_median_noncoastal = median_non_coastnative,
           alpha_median_coastal = median_coastnative) %>%
    select(-adjusted_OHI, -alpha_median, -eta_median, -base_rank, -adjusted_rank)

# Calculate adjusted OHI scores
extdata_fig4_c_data <- extdata_fig4_c_data %>%
    group_by(country) %>%
    mutate(OHI_noncoastalpref = calculate_OHI_score(alpha_median_noncoastal, goal_score, eta_median_noncoastal),
           OHI_coastalpref = calculate_OHI_score(alpha_median_coastal, goal_score, eta_median_coastal)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    distinct(country, .keep_all = TRUE)

extdata_fig4_c <- plot_ohi_density_panel(
    extdata_fig4_c_data %>% mutate(adjusted_OHI = OHI_coastalpref),
    "Only coastal-affine participants (>10 days at sea)", pct_x = 62)

#### SI Appendix Fig. S4d: Mean instead of median aggregation of alpha and eta
# Mean-aggregating the block-level eta is degenerate: the Tobit eta estimates have an
# extreme right tail, so their sample mean diverges (~1e11, vs a median of ~2.8) and the
# CES aggregator collapses to its Leontief limit. We therefore set each country's adjusted
# OHI to the minimum of its ten goal scores (the eta -> Inf limit, in which the alpha
# weights drop out). The divergent mean eta is printed for reporting in the text.
eta_total_sample_mean <- mean(ohi_estimates_online$eta, na.rm = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("Fig.4d mean-aggregation: mean eta = %s (median eta = %.2f) -> Leontief (min goal score)\n",
            format(eta_total_sample_mean, scientific = TRUE, digits = 4), eta_total_sample))

extdata_fig4_d_data <- OHI_table %>%
    group_by(country) %>%
    mutate(adjusted_OHI = min(goal_score, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    distinct(country, .keep_all = TRUE)

extdata_fig4_d <- plot_ohi_density_panel(extdata_fig4_d_data,
    "Mean preferences instead of median preferences", pct_x = 52)
```
